newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: McCollam chairman says bid "reasonable".
newsitem.headline: McCollam chairman says bid "reasonable".

text.p: McCollam Printers Ltd's chairman Brian Allison said on Monday that at first glance Blue Star's $2.75 per share takeover offer appeared reasonable.
"I think it is a reasonable offer, whether it proves outstanding is something we have yet to determine," he told Reuters.
"It's an offer we are taking seriously."
He said earlier the company had formed a committee of independent directors with Andrew Harmos to consider the offer.
They have appointed Merrill Lynch as advisers and Allison expects to report back their advice within three weeks.

Allison said McCollam was an excellent company in good shape, adding the offer was a suprise as far as the independent directors were concerned but he assumed the McCollam family, which controls 38 percent, had had discussions.
The company share price rose 42 cents to $2.72 on Monday morning. Some 79,000 shares were traded.

The offer is conditional on the McCollam family accepting the bid. They are being offered scrip at the equivalent of $3.00 per share, which Allison said recognised a premium for the controlling holding and risks associated with accepting scrip.
Blue Star is a unit of U.S. Office Products Co.
